newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court delays ruling on mercenary Denard.
newsitem.headline: French court delays ruling on mercenary Denard.

text.p: A Paris court postponed a decision on Monday on whether soldier of fortune Bob Denard should face trial over the 1989 murder of Comoros President Ahmed Abdallah during a coup d'etat on the tiny Indian Ocean archipelago.
Denard, 67, was arrested last year in the Comoros islands after his third mercenary raid there and jailed in Paris. He was released in July.
Judge Martine Anzani said information provided by the investigating magistrate was insufficient for a ruling and asked the magistrate for a map of the presidential palace where Abdallah was killed.
Denard, who had led the 1978 invasion that put Abdallah in power, is accused of complicity in his murder. Investigators believe the killing was carried out by Denard's men in the presidential guard.
Two of his lieutenants, Jean-Paul Guerrier and Dominique Malacrino, are also suspects in the case.
Denard is also under investigation for his third invasion, when he overthrew president Mohamed Said Djohar last year.

He was defeated a week later when French troops landed and arrested him and his 30 white mercenaries, most of whom were paid $25,000 for their services. Twenty of them are under investigation over involvement in the coup.
The French troops, however, did not return Djohar to power. Mohamed Taki is now president of the archipelago, with France's backing.
Denard asserts that France approved of his interventions in Comoros.
